newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Papers buying rival in $674 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Papers buying rival in $674 mln deal.

text.p: Consolidated Papers Inc. agreed on Wednesday to buy the Wisconsin paper operations of troubled Canadian paper maker Repap Eneterprises Inc. in a $674 million deal that will strengthen its position as the biggest U.S. producer of coated printing paper.

Consolidated Papers will pay $227 million in cash and assume $447 million in debt to buy Repap Wisconsin Inc., a Kimberly, Wis., maker of coated papers. Repap Wisconsin is wholly owned by Repap Enterprises, a Montreal-based paper maker that has been hit in recent years by heavy debts and weak demand for coated paper.
In March, Repap's British Columbia pulp-making unit sought protection from creditors.

Repap Wisconsin, with capacity to make 508,000 tons of coated paper a year, had 1996 sales of $405 million and about 1,000 employees. Its papers are used in brochures, advertising inserts, annual reports, catalogs and magazines.

Consolidated Papers, with annual capacity of 1.3 million tons of coated paper, earned $179 million or $4.01 a share, on sales of $1.5 billion last year. The company, which has 6,000 workers, is based in Wisconsin Rapids, about 100 miles from the operations of Repap Wisconsin.

"This acquisition expands our presence in the coated paper marketplace (and) positions us to better serve existing and new customers," Consolidated President Gorton Evans said in a statement. "The products they produce are consistent with the type and quality of the coated papers we already make."
The transaction, which is expected to close in the third quarter, includes Repap Wisconsin's sales and marketing affiliate, a groundwood pulp mill and a paper recycling facility.

Analyst Brian Topp of BZW Canada said Repap got a good price for its Wisconsin operations. "I was pleasantly surprised by how much money they got. It was certainly in excess of what I thought they would receive," Topp said.

Repap said it also agreed to sell other paper and lumber operations in The Pas, Manitoba, to Tolko Industries Ltd., a closely held company based in British Columbia. Terms were not disclosed, but Repap officials said they expected the sale price to exceed the unit's C$95 million ($68 million) of debt.
Repap officials said the company would continue to operate its facilities in the Canadian province of New Brunswick, after judging bids for that unit too low.
Repap New Brunswick, which includes a 492,000-ton coated paper mill, and makes kraft and groundwood pulp, carries C$1 billion ($720 million) of debt.

Repap Chief Financial Officer Ronald Sumner told reporters he did not expect Repap New Brunswick to file for court protection from creditors, but rather be recapitalized as paper market conditions improved.
"There are a number of successful one-mill companies and we expect this to be one," he said.
Consolidated Papers also makes paperboard, paperboard products, corrugated displays and containers. Its stock fell 18.75 cents to $56.437 on the New York Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
Repap Enterprises stock rose C12 cents to C50 cents on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
